notes:
Summary:
- CustomerFlow builds a SaaS support platform used by mid-market+ enterprises; primary product is an agent-assist/ticket-deflection module. They ingest KB articles, historical tickets, and conversation transcripts into a RAG pipeline.
- Goal: reduce live-agent escalations by 35% with high-quality top-5 answers; strict latency SLOs for agent UX and embedded widgets.

Current environment / scale:
- Index scope: ~5M passages (KB articles + ticket snippets + transcripts), avg passage ~200 tokens. Expect growth to 8-10M in 12 months.
- Query volume: peak 600 qps across regions (NA/EU), steady-state 120 qps.
- Existing infra: in-house retrieval + Elastic search embeddings prototype; memory/ops costs rising.

Technical requirements / priorities:
- Primary: embeddings-based retrieval + reranking for top-5 quality. They need recall@5 >= 0.88 and precision in top-5 to meaningfully deflect tickets.
- Latency: end-to-end retrieval+rerank widget SLO p95 <= 200ms (hard), p50 target <= 80ms. Mobile/embedded widget requires low tail latency.
- Cost: target amortized cost-per-query <= $0.004 (including candidate generation + cross-encoder rerank).
- Indexing: incremental updates, realtime ingest for new KB articles and ticket triage, compact vector store with sharding across regions.
- Models: prefer open/quantized models for reranker (intent: use mid-size cross-encoders or distilled rankers). Open to Redwood recommendations (quantized L2 or 4-bit).
- Routing/fallbacks: require regional routing (EU data residency) and fallback to smaller models when capacity constrained (graceful degradation).
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, audit logs, KMS-managed keys, optional VPC/private control plane.

POC notes (evaluation):
- POC started 2025-01-20. Redwood provided two-stage design: ANN bi-encoder candidate gen (FAISS/HNSW on quantized vectors) -> lightweight cross-encoder rerank on top-10.
- Baseline metrics from CustomerFlow prototype: recall@5 0.82, p95 latency 260ms (cross-encoder on CPU), cost ~$0.007/query.
- Redwood POC run (dedicated GPU small pool): recall@5 0.89 (meets target), end-to-end p95 185ms (with batching + KV-cache on prefix queries), cost estimated $0.0035/query with quantized models and dynamic batching.
- Demo call 2025-01-28 with support-product team, recorded (Fireflies ff_2025-01-28_01_custflow_poc-demo).

Sales/technical feedback:
- Positive: clear improvement in recall and latency vs prototype, Redwood console visibility on per-route cost/latency is helpful.
- Concerns: need written guarantees for EU data residency and audit logs; legal asked for KMS/HSM architecture diagram. Also want a failover path to a lower-cost routing tier during peak.

Next steps (short):
- Deliver KMS/HSM integration design by 2025-02-20 (SE: Priya).
- Run extended POC 2-week stress test: 8M vector index, sustained 600 qps across 2 regions to validate autoscaling & p95 tail. Redwood to provide test plan and cost model.
- Legal/security to review SOC2 + ISO-like docs; provide copies to CustomerFlow security team.

Representative quotes from demo:
- "Top-5 results finally match what our triage team needs — we can automate suggested articles for the majority of cases."
- "We need the p95 latency number in writing before procurement can sign off."

Attachments / artifacts: pricing deck, POC report draft, security questionnaire in Drive.
